issues.body: `sketch_predicate` passes `(o, vector(o))` to `pool_weighted`, so the weight comes from metadata about the object entity. The design and existing `pool_weighted` contract define the key as the subject/head whose provenance qualifies the asserted value. Provenance attached to `ex:dubious` does not establish that the separate `ex:hub ex:cites ex:dubious` assertion is dubious. The new prose acknowledges and then changes this load-bearing meaning, producing a heuristic with different semantics rather than wiring `w(t)`. The test is therefore non-vacuous mechanically but validates the wrong invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Represent or resolve provenance for each `(node, predicate, object)` assertion and pass the identifier whose provenance actually qualifies that assertion. If plain RDF cannot distinguish statement provenance, keep the uniform/no-op behavior or require an explicit reified/RDF-star provenance mapping; do not infer assertion confidence from the object entity's metadata. Replace the test fixture with two independently provenance-qualified edge assertions.
issues.title: Pooling weights entity provenance, not the asserted edge's provenance

issues.body: `predicate_block_weight` scans every triple with a predicate and stores their global mean in a shared `SchemaHeader`. That same multiplier is then returned for every grounded node, including nodes with no incident edge for that predicate. This contradicts the claimed design invariant that query-time scaling of a node's modality is derived from that node's incident-edge provenance. The end-to-end test hides the defect: it grounds `ex:solid` but gives its second block the weight derived solely from `ex:shaky ex:weak ex:y`, an edge not incident to `ex:solid`.
issues.fix_hint: Compute weights at the node/block grounding boundary from that node's contributing edges, or introduce per-row/per-node weight storage if persistence is required. Do not put node-specific provenance into a graph-global schema header. Update the test so each returned weight is derived from the grounded node's actual block contributions and add a second node with different provenance to prove weights are not globally shared.
issues.title: A global predicate average cannot provide per-node incident-edge fusion weights

issues.body: The new text states that the training axis has a positive MRR delta clearing 2·se and that pooling has no measured lift at any blend. These are empirical performance outcomes from an unspecified work-box run, not stable API behavior or canonical checked evidence. The repository contract explicitly forbids hard-coded performance numbers and treats work-box/session results as non-canonical; encoding the conclusion in a public skill also risks becoming false as code, seeds, or fixtures change.
issues.fix_hint: Describe how to run the instrument and how to interpret its returned statistics without asserting the current observed outcome. If a canonical result is required, route it through the repository's approved benchmark artifact/ratchet and cite that generated evidence rather than hard-coding a local run's conclusion.
issues.title: Documentation publishes non-canonical measured performance conclusions

verdict.summary: The new callers do not implement the documented per-triple/incident-edge provenance semantics. Pooling substitutes each object neighbour's own entity provenance for the provenance of the edge assertion, while header weighting computes one graph-global predicate weight and applies it to every node. The end-to-end tests encode those substitutions rather than validating the design invariant. The skill also publishes a session-specific measured outcome, contrary to the repository's non-canonical performance-evidence rule.
